root_cause.text: The DSA switch probing code mismanaged conduit net_device lifetime by keeping only the underlying device/kobject reference from OF/non-OF lookup instead of a proper long-lived netdev reference, leaving leaked kobject refs in the OF path and allowing stale cpu_dp->conduit pointers if the conduit unregistered.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “the OF path... never releases the elevated refcount on the conduit's kobject” and that “Holding the net device's underlying kobject isn't actually of much help... What helps us to prevent the net device from being unregistered is the parallel netdev reference mechanism”; correspondingly, the patch adds netdevice_tracker to struct dsa_port, acquires references with netdev_hold() under rtnl_lock() in both dsa_port_parse_of() and dsa_port_parse(), releases the kobject with put_device(), and balances the lifetime with netdev_put() in error, release, and shutdown paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add netdevice tracking state to dsa_port so conduit device references can be tracked per port.
intent_record.what: A new field named conduit_tracker of type netdevice_tracker was added to struct dsa_port, inserted after the phylink configuration member.
intent_record.how: This extends each dsa_port instance with storage for tracking an associated net_device reference through the netdevice tracking mechanism, enabling later code to record and manage that relationship at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DSA OF port parsing to safely acquire and release conduit netdev references under RTNL during CPU port setup.
intent_record.what: The change adds an `int err` variable, wraps `of_find_net_device_by_node(ethernet)` with `rtnl_lock()`/`rtnl_unlock()`, returns `-EPROBE_DEFER` only after unlocking when no net device is found, adds `netdev_hold(conduit, &dp->conduit_tracker, GFP_KERNEL)` and `put_device(&conduit->dev)` after locating the conduit, changes the direct return of `dsa_port_parse_cpu(dp, conduit, user_protocol)` into storing its result in `err`, and conditionally calls `netdev_put(conduit, &dp->conduit_tracker)` on error before returning `err`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the net device lookup and reference handling are done under RTNL protection, converts the found conduit device reference into an explicitly tracked netdev hold, releases the temporary device reference from the lookup, and drops the held netdev reference if CPU port parsing fails. This prevents reference lifetime and locking issues while preserving deferred probing when the conduit is not yet available.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix CPU port parsing to safely acquire and track the conduit net_device reference under RTNL and release it on parse failure.
intent_record.what: The patch removes the helper function dsa_dev_to_net_device() and inlines its logic into the "cpu" branch of dsa_port_parse(). The new code adds local variables for a struct device pointer and an error code, wraps the net-device lookup with rtnl_lock()/rtnl_unlock(), changes the device reference handling from dev_hold()/dev_put() to netdev_hold(conduit, &dp->conduit_tracker, GFP_KERNEL) and netdev_put(conduit, &dp->conduit_tracker), and now stores the result of dsa_port_parse_cpu() so the netdev reference is released on error.
intent_record.how: At runtime, CPU port parsing now acquires the RTNL lock while locating and converting the child "net" device, uses tracked netdev reference management tied to dp->conduit_tracker, and ensures the held conduit reference is dropped if dsa_port_parse_cpu() fails. This avoids untracked or improperly balanced net_device references during parsing and makes the lookup/reference sequence safer under networking core synchronization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release conduit netdevice references for CPU ports during DSA switch port cleanup to prevent refcount leaks.
intent_record.what: In dsa_switch_release_ports(), a new conditional block was added at the start of the per-port cleanup loop that checks whether the current port is a CPU port and has a non-NULL conduit, and if so calls netdev_put(dp->conduit, &dp->conduit_tracker).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this releases the held reference to the conduit netdevice for CPU ports during switch port teardown, preventing the conduit device reference from being leaked when ports are released.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release each CPU port conduit netdevice reference during switch shutdown after disconnecting its DSA pointer.
intent_record.what: The loop over CPU ports in dsa_switch_shutdown() was changed from a single-statement form to a block, keeping the existing assignment of dp->conduit->dsa_ptr = NULL and adding a new call to netdev_put(dp->conduit, &dp->conduit_tracker) inside the loop.
intent_record.how: At shutdown, each CPU port's conduit netdevice reference is now explicitly released after clearing its dsa_ptr link, preventing the conduit netdevice from retaining an unreleased reference and ensuring proper lifetime and cleanup behavior.
